artists.biography: James is a British rock band from Manchester, England. They formed in 1982 and were active throughout the 1980s, but most successful during the 1990s. Their hit singles include "Come Home", "Sit Down", and "She's a Star" as well as their American college radio hit "Laid". Following the departure of lead singer Tim Booth in 2001, the band became inactive but re-formed in January 2007, returning for a new album and international tour. Up to 2010, the band had sold more than 25 million albums worldwide.

perplexity.description:
Living in Extraordinary Times is the 15th studio album by British rock band James, released on 3 August 2018 through Infectious Music. The album marks a continuation of the band’s evolution, blending their signature indie rock sound with contemporary social commentary and personal reflection. Produced by Mercury and Brit Award winner Charlie Andrew and Beni Giles, the record features a fusion of urgent guitar-driven tracks and atmospheric textures, exploring themes ranging from political frustration to intimate family moments. Notable songs like "Hank" and "Coming Home (Pt. 2)" showcase the band’s ability to merge pointed lyrics with melodic depth, the latter featuring keyboard contributions from longtime collaborator Brian Eno.

As a follow-up to their successful 2016 album Girl at the End of the World, Living in Extraordinary Times reaffirms James’ relevance in the modern rock landscape. The album received generally positive reviews from critics, who praised its ambition and willingness to challenge expectations, while also noting its cohesive blend of energy and introspection. Commercially, it peaked at number six on the UK Albums Chart and also charted in Belgium and Portugal, underscoring the band’s enduring appeal. With its striking artwork by Magnus Gjoen and a mix of studio experimentation and live vitality, the album stands as a significant entry in James’ extensive discography.
